title: Housing Vacancies and Homeownership (CPS/HVS, Third Quarter 2026 data), 10:00 a.m. ET, FOMC decision day
source: CENSUS: two independent census.gov primaries fetched direct 2026-09-06. (1) economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html (HTTP 200, 91,396 bytes), row "Housing Vacancies and Homeownership | October 28, 2026 | 10:00 AM | Third Quarter 2026", release code A202610281000, reference A202603. (2) housing/hvs/files/currenthvspress.pdf (HTTP 200, 722,443 bytes) — the LIVE release itself, CB26-116, "Quarterly Residential Vacancies and Homeownership, Second Quarter 2026", released 2026-07-28, whose summary box reads "Next release: October 28, 2026". That is the program stating its own next date, the same shape of second primary the new-home-sales-2026-10-27 lane used. Promoted from the new-home-sales-2026-10-27 lane's `estimate` proposal by this event's own initial research, on the precedent that lane set: the no-self-confirm convention binds the discovering sweep, not the independent second look. The series has never been suspended — 28 consecutive quarterly rows, reference quarters 2019-Q4 through 2026-Q3, zero gaps, parsed from eight Census calendars (1,128 unique rows, cal-2019 through cal-2026). The release time is stated on the calendar row and not on the PDF. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: DISCOVERED by the new-home-sales-2026-10-27 adjacency sweep as the STOCK-side read of the housing market this calendar otherwise tracks only as flow. Initial research 2026-09-06 confirms the date and then finds what separates this print from every other macro row on the board: it is the calendar's most Fed-collided release. Its quarterly slot (late Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct into early Feb/May/Aug/Nov) is the same window the FOMC's Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct meetings occupy, so 13 of the 24 HVS releases since 2021-01-27 (54.2%) landed on an FOMC decision day or its eve, and 2026-10-28 is only the THIRD decision-day landing (after 2022-11-02 and 2023-05-03). Measured on Yahoo daily bars across twelve instruments (SPY QQQ ITB XHB DHI LEN PHM TOL AMH INVH MAA UDR), the release itself is a null: 27 release sessions since 2020-01-30, nothing survives a Holm correction (best adjusted p=0.252, UDR), and collided-vs-clean release days are indistinguishable (best adjusted p=0.138). The DECISION day is loud on the same bars and the same method: 45 sessions, 9 of 12 instruments survive Holm at 0.05 (ITB 3.100% vs a 1.992% baseline, XHB/DHI/PHM/TOL/LEN all adjusted p<0.001, and the rental REITs too — AMH adjusted p=0.003, UDR 0.0088). Not a GDPNow trigger: zero "vacanc"/"homeowner" hits across the 83 PostedUpdates and 120 InternalUpdates rows of GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx; 2026-10-28's nowcast row is the FINAL Q3 nowcast at 08:30, triggered by the Advance Economic Indicators report 90 minutes BEFORE this print. So the day's sequence is 08:30 AEI + final Q3 GDPNow, 10:00 this print, 14:00 the Fed — the print is sandwiched and unreadable. Substantively it corroborates the proposer's inventory-overhang read from the occupied stock: rental vacancy 7.3% (no quarter since 2017Q3 has printed above it), homeowner vacancy 1.2% (joint highest since 2019Q4), homeownership 65.0% (no quarter since 2019Q3 has printed below it), South rental vacancy 9.5%, all from CB26-116. But the publisher itself flags the movement as noise: CB26-116 says "not statistically different" 16 times and "virtually the same" 3 times against 4 "was higher than" and 1 "was lower than", and its own stated standard error on the rental vacancy rate (0.149pp, 90% MOE +/-0.245pp) is LARGER than the 0.20pp median quarter-over-quarter move of the last 40 quarters. Impact LOW, symbols empty: no house playbook is macro/housing-keyed (0 hits re-grepped 2026-09-06 across trade-playbooks.md and multi-symbol-sweep.md) and no instrument attaches.
